A dollar coin that my calc teacher gave us the day before graduation. I figure if there's anything I ever needed luck for, math would be it.

I lost it this past November or so, but I carried mine for over 15 years.

It was a 1965 silver quarter.

What was special about it to me, though, is the circumstances in which I obtained it.

When I was 16, a bunch of us kids would go to this country store and play pool and hang out and whatnot. One day when I went to exchange a dollar for some quarters, one of the ones I received had a small hole drilled right on top of Washington's head. Then I realised that it made a different sound than a regular coin when shaken against others.

I kept it and went home that night and looked it up on the net and found that it was a silver quarter. Neat.

The next day at school during one of our breaks, I was at the vending machine and before I knew what I was doing, I put the quarter in for some chips. At the time, I wasn't a really big loss, but I was a bit bummed about it. Oh well.

A couple of weeks later back at the store with friends, I went to the counter to get quarters. One of them was the same quarter, same hole right on top of Washington's head.

This time, I put the quarter in my left pocket away from my normal change. When I got home, I took a knife and carved the hole just enough to where it could fit on the single bar section of my key chain ring.

There it stayed for many years.

I never really looked at it much, but it was always there. I think the last time I closely examined it was sometime in 2014. Years of being on the ring had slowly worn the hole much bigger, so at some point it was able to fit around the double bar section of my ring and I noticed that the hole was approaching the edge of the quarter.

Then at some point last year, it was just gone. I know it was in the last half of the year because I remember seeing it in the summer.
